data.gender_notes: Ashwath is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Ashwath is a Sanskrit name derived from the word 'ashva' meaning 'horse'. This name is believed to be the vehicle of the gods and is often associated with strength, power, and divine blessings. In Hindu mythology, the Ashvins are a pair of divine twins who are the gods of healing, herbs, horses, and the sky. The name Ashwath carries the meaning “Horse, Vehicle of Gods” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Ashwath usually hope their child will grow to embody horse, vehicle of gods and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A symbol of divine grace and strength.
data.etymology: Ashwath belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Horse, Vehicle of Gods.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Ashwath total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

data.cultural_impact: The name Ashwath carries a rich cultural significance in Hinduism, where it is believed that the Ashavins, the divine twins associated with this name, bestow strength, power, and good health. The Ashavins were also considered deities of agriculture, and their blessings were believed to lead to prosperous harvests. Therefore, the name is also connected to the importance of horses and agriculture in Indian culture.
data.spiritual_significance: Ashwath holds great spiritual significance as it is the symbol of divine grace, power, and the offering of protection. The name represents the idea of the divine being extremely close and accessible to the devotee. Ashwath embodies the energy of the gods and their blessings, thereby ensuring the spiritual growth and well-being of the one who bears the name. Additionally, the name is also connected to the idea of the journey of life, symbolizing that the divine is by one's side throughout the ups and downs of life.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Ashwath symbolizes steadfastness and longevity, derived from the Ashvattha Tree - a symbol of immortality and eternal life in Hindu mythology. Its roots represent the past, trunk the present, and leaves the future, signifying the continuity of life.
